purpose: Determine whether learning support transfer during early supine recovery addresses the persistent lean observed by 3 seconds.
observable_pose_rule: Classify the actual release pose using the already checked first policy gravity observation. Keep the right-side branch separate.
initial_design: Compare the fixed recovery parent with a single early support progress change on actual supine worlds. Audit upright rotation, physical foot support, and head-leg contact together before selecting a learning signal. Keep all-pose recovery and final holding as the outcome.
candidate_signal: From 2.3 through 3.0 seconds, multiply bounded progress toward the original tilt limit by foot-contact fraction and head-leg clearance. Activate only when the first released policy gravity observation classifies the episode as supine. All components outside this window retain their original values.
preflight_gates: Recompute native contact flags and body rotation at the recorded control times in both development releases. Quantify event order by scene and preserve variation across releases. Obtain a substep recording if finer ordering is needed.

Validate the candidate signal against contact-on stalled cases and useful temporary support during successful recoveries. Reject signals that reward the wrong support phase or require future observations at runtime.

Check the reward-stage event clock, first policy observation latch, selective reset and same-instant native contact readback before evaluating a new value target. The saved signal has no reward or actor update authority.
Check observation, action, and state reset/restore semantics, bounded joint targets and retained parent behavior on the other poses before physical controls.

Freeze fresh development seeds, original per-pose timing/holding thresholds, action guards, matched sample budget, checkpoint provenance and zero-step VRAM before learning. Use the previously selected 3072-environment capacity only after the new zero-step check.
